title: Transferable Energy-Latency Attacks via Repetitive Generation
one_line_claim: LoopLLM induces catastrophic looping in LLMs through prompt optimization that exploits autoregressive vulnerabilities to achieve >90% of maximum generation length compared to 20% baseline.
method_summary: LoopLLM optimizes a repetition-inducing suffix using cycle loss to minimize output entropy and reinforce repetitive token generation, with token-aligned ensemble optimization for cross-model transferability. The approach uses gradient-based token search to construct prefixes that exploit autoregressive vulnerabilities. Empirically, the method achieves dramatic output extension and transferability without white-box access.

key_findings.finding: LoopLLM achieves over 90% of maximum output length compared to 20% for baselines on 12 open-source LLMs.
key_findings.quote: LoopLLM achieves >90% of the maximum output length compared to 20% in the baseline.

key_findings.finding: Token-aligned ensemble optimization improves transferability by 40% to newer models like DeepSeek-V3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
key_findings.quote: token-aligned ensemble optimization improves transferability by 40% to newer models.

key_findings.finding: Simple entropy-based filtering defenses are ineffective; LoopLLM evades them by generating plausible-looking but repetitive text that maintains low entropy.
key_findings.quote: Our defense evaluation reveals that simple entropy-based filtering can be easily evaded, highlighting the practical threat of LoopLLM.

limitations: Requires optimization time per target or ensemble; real-time attack constraints not discussed.
Focuses on inducing looping but does not address detection or mitigation beyond entropy filtering.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both are concerned with catastrophic failure modes in LLMs (looping, non-termination, extreme output length), and both operate on per-token signals to detect or induce these failures.
differs_on: LoopLLM focuses on adversarial attack generation (forcing failures through prompt optimization); HERALD focuses on predictive detection of naturally-occurring compression-induced catastrophes.
LoopLLM exploits prompt-level vulnerabilities and high-level decoding dynamics; HERALD uses fine-grained logit distributions under KV-cache compression.
LoopLLM's threat model assumes an attacker constructing adversarial prompts; HERALD's model assumes passive observation during normal (unattacked) inference.
